newsitem.title: USA: UPS, Teamsters recess, more talks Friday.
newsitem.headline: UPS, Teamsters recess, more talks Friday.

text.p: United Parcel Service and Teamsters officials agreed to recess for several hours and resume talks aimed at settling the 12-day-old strike later Friday, a spokesman for the federal mediator guiding the talks said.

"There are some serious numbers to be crunched. It's going to take several hours. When the work is done, they will reconvene," said Dave Helfert, spokesman for the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service.
The two sides agreed to take a break and rest at around 1:45 a.m. EDT Friday, and Helfert said the mathematical analysis would likely take two to three hours.
"The fact that they are crunching numbers tells me they are dealing in detailed issues," said Helfert, when asked if the discussions had moved into the realm of formal negotiations.

Helfert, speaking to reporters at a Capitol Hill hotel where the two sides began their marathon talks just after 9 a.m. EDT Thursday, described the mindset of the negotiators as "tired and determined."

The talks to end the strike, one of the biggest U.S. work stoppages in over a quarter century, appeared to moving forward after signals from UPS Chairman James Kelly Thursday that the company might be more open to compromise.
